sources: USNI News, 'October Marks Highest Number of Strait of Hormuz Attacks' (Oct 22), drawing on IMO attack tally, Lloyd's List maritime-intelligence transit data, Washington Institute fellow Noam Raydan
fault_line: Is Iran's ship-hitting campaign a rational blockade strategy, or economic self-harm that justifies a US/Israeli escalation after the midterms?

sections.what_happened: October 2026 has seen 27 attacks on commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz per the IMO -- the highest monthly total since the Iran-US war began Feb 28 (22 attacks in March, the previous high). Between Oct 5-11, 104 non-Iranian-linked vessels still transited (12 attacks that week, 6 on Oct 11 alone); weekly transits fell from 126 the prior week but remained 31% above August's weekly average. Raydan: Iran's aim is not to hit specific ships but to keep the southern route 'very unsafe' and risk premiums high; the US has also disabled ships as part of its two-part blockade.
sections.what_verified: IMO tally via USNI; Lloyd's List transit counts; Raydan on-the-record at Lloyd's List Outlook Forum (New York, Oct 21).
sections.what_disputed: Methodology differences across sources: straits.live citing IMF PortWatch records only 4 transits on Oct 18 vs 85/day pre-crisis baseline (AIS-based; excludes vessels within 25 km of a working port; 170 vessels holding position). Iran's IRGC claims higher ship-hit counts (7 ships Oct 22) that could not be independently verified; Trump accused Tehran of faking hits.
sections.why_matters: The numbers behind the most dangerous month in the Strait: 27 attacks in October -- a record. Ships still sail, but every one of them sails through a war zone. And Iran says it has no reason to stop.
sections.context: Background: NEW (big-missed, published Oct 22) -- USNI News: October is the highest-attack month in Hormuz since the Feb war began -- 27 ship attacks per IMO

totw_analysis: Our read: The numbers behind the most dangerous month in the Strait: 27 attacks in October -- a record. Ships still sail, but every one of them sails through a war zone. And Iran says it has no reason to stop. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is Iran's ship-hitting campaign a rational blockade strategy, or economic self-harm that justifies a US/Israeli escalation after the midterms?
